chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who enters Mecca with women whom he has ordered to perform Tamattu' before Tarwiyah by one or two or three days, and he fears menstruation for some of them. He said: 'When they have completed their Tamattu' and have exited the state of Ihram, let him look at the one for whom he fears menstruation, and order her to perform Ghusl and enter Ihram for Hajj in her place. Then she should perform Tawaf with the House, and with As-Safa and Al-Marwah. If something happens to her [i.e., menstruation], she will complete the rest of the rituals while she is a Hayd (menstruating woman).'

I said to him: 'Is not the Tawaf of the women still remaining?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then is she held in pledge until she finishes it?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Then why does he not leave her until she completes her rituals?' He said: 'One ritual remains upon her which is easier for her than all the rituals remaining upon her, out of fear of menstruation.'

I said: 'Does the husband not leave her and the companions?' He said: 'It is not for them to do that; she is held in pledge against them until he leaves her until she becomes pure and completes the rituals.'
And that which indicates the permissibility of the precedence of the women's Tawaf with necessity is what they narrated:

key_terms.أَحْلَلْنَ: They exited the state of Ihram
key_terms.التَّرْوِيَة: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, a key date in Hajj rituals
key_terms.تَقَدُّمُ طَوَافِ النِّسَاءِ: The precedence/early performance of the women's Tawaf
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: The Tawaf of the women (specifically referring to the remaining Tawaf)
key_terms.فَتَمَتَّعْنَ: They performed Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who starts menstruating during the middle of her Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Rida (AS) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the practical dilemma of menstrual interruption during Tamattu' Hajj, prioritizing the completion of essential rites over strict chronological order. It establishes that the menstruating woman may perform Tawaf al-Nisa’ and Sa'i while still in her state of hayd, thereby avoiding the burden of delaying all rituals until full purity is restored. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of facilitating worship by allowing partial completion of obligations even in states of ritual impurity.
